key_insight: Selective Floquet coupling to two auxiliary transmon states enables simulated CZ gates with average fidelities above 99.99%.
engineering_relevance: Using higher transmon levels as controlled interaction pathways offers additional options for engineering high-fidelity entangling gates.
method: Parametric modulation couples |11⟩ to |02⟩ and |20⟩ while suppressing leading |01⟩–|10⟩ exchange.
Implement CZ gates through nonadiabatic bright-state round trips or adiabatic zero-energy dark-state evolution.
Control modulation phase to realize conventional and unconventional geometric CZ gates.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations report average fidelities above 99.99% for both core protocols; effective-model tests favor unconventional geometric control under selected errors, and spectator-qubit simulations retain high fidelities.
watch_item: Experimental validation remains necessary to establish performance under realistic modulation imperfections, decoherence, and leakage.
paper_title: Controlled-Z Gates via Floquet Coupling to Two Auxiliary States in Transmon Circuits
